newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar the key as German bulls keep on running.
newsitem.headline: Dollar the key as German bulls keep on running.

text.p: Germany's DAX index traded near record highs on Wednesday, keeping up its advance after Tuesday's steamrollering bull-run, with the sturdy U.S. dollar still the main engine driving gains and no correction in sight.
In mid-session bourse trade, the DAX index was just off record highs at 3,344.31 points, up 0.71 percent or 23.65.
Dealers expressed their admiration for the resilience of the bull-run in the face of some hardly inspirational fundamental factors.
These included sluggish German GDP data, downbeat January industrial orders, a lower Wall Street overnight and a softer German debt market.

The strength of the dollar at 1.71 marks, in or around 34 month highs and seemingly unstoppable at the moment, was viewed by market players as a panacea for any wobbles, woes or potential jitters in the German share market.
The market shrugged off worries of unspectacular economic growth after fourth quarter Gross Domestic Product figures showed only a 0.1 percent rise, up 2.2 percent from the year-earlier quarter.
While the figure was a shade higher than expected, it hardly indicated a vigorous recovery, but did not overly affect sentiment.

What could have been a double whammy for the market came with further bad news on the macroeconomic front after German January industry output figures showed a 1.7 percent drop, mainly driven by a 25 percent month-on-month drop in the construction industry.
Again, the market took this in its stride in mid-session bourse and the market stayed steady.
Earlier factors included a nearly one-percent lower close on the Dow Jones Index overnight and downbeat German debt all contributed to early fears of a consolidation, if not a full-blown correction.

Dealers breathed a sigh of relief when early electronic trade on the IBIS DAX index was stable. "If a correction was going to happen it probably would have happened by now," said one Frankfurt trader.
Indeed, early lacklustre electronic trade early on soon turned to another assault on record highs when the index hit 3,349.94 points.
Shares in the limelight included Deutsche Lufthansa AG, which was up 4.87 percent at 24.12 marks in mid-session bourse trade.
Traders had identified a large domestic buyer who was buying "massive" amounts of the stock. The stock was lifted by a Boeing report which forecast a 4.4 percent increase in air travel in Europe.
Diversified utility Veba AG was also higher early on, up 1.45 marks at 99.45 marks, as technical factors buoyed the stock.
Tyre-maker Continental AG was up 90 pfennigs at 34.70 marks after it said its 1996 pre-tax profits were up 68.2 percent at 328 million marks.
